challenge.better_approach: Looked at (a) updating the text pin to the new grep line. That's one line, but the next reshape of bin/cairn reds it again, and it stays a reach into bin's source; (b) calling cairn.tools.rack.folder_of, which the proof already checks separately and which is not bin/cairn's lookup. Running the command is the only measure of bin/cairn's behaviour that is bin's public interface.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That bin/cairn's earlier wiring branches (bin/cairn:193, 304, 387) write only under CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT, so a scratch root keeps the run off live ~/.cairn. The builder runs it twice under the tester seal and checks that the live ~/.cairn/devices/inferenceproxy is unchanged. Also assumed: an unrecognised word at instance 0 reaches CAIRN_BUS_MOUTH. bin/cairn:417-418 says so.
challenge.prior_art: bin/proofs/test_a_declared_instance_is_wired_by_the_command.py and cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word.py already run bin/cairn under a scratch instance root and a stand-in CAIRN_BUS_MOUTH. This tooth follows that idiom. The same proof's 'the recipe moves instance-space once' tooth already uses scratch_dir for a HOME.
challenge.real_collision: f942a413f26d owns the proof's existing teeth and is PROVED. Removing one check() line inside its tooth 1 removes no tooth function, so rung 4 sees no tooth removed. The why names the replacement. 78a600419a21 is PROVED and unchanged.

answers.falsifier: RED if 'cairn inference <word>' in a scratch HOME does not run inferenceproxy's instance-bin word, or a scriptless word does not reach the bus mouth as 'inference', or the proof still reads bin/cairn's text. Horizon: both inferenceproxy proofs reseal green, then c620e551970f walks.
answers.from_idea: none, because the red was measured live: cairn/devices/inferenceproxy/proofs/test_the_proxy_stands_at_its_outline_address.py tooth 'bin/cairn maps a typed answers_as to its folder' reds at the Linux reseal committed in cairn f9020855d (2026-11-18), after 78a600419a21's land at 732da454b reshaped bin/cairn's lookup (bin/cairn:353)
answers.how: In cairn/devices/inferenceproxy/proofs/test_the_proxy_stands_at_its_outline_address.py, drop the check that greps bin/cairn's text and add one tooth that runs the real bin/cairn under a scratch HOME (CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT under it): a probe script at inferenceproxy/0/bin/<word> answers 'cairn inference <word>', and a word with no script reaches a stand-in CAIRN_BUS_MOUTH as 'inference <word>'. Nothing of bin's internals is imported (RULE 1). Keyed under this ticket in PROVES; f942a413f26d's entry stays.
answers.traces_to: Law 9 (red is the default; green is earned): both inferenceproxy proofs stand red on this check. RULE 1: a proof that pins another component's source text is coupled to its internals, so a change confined to bin reds inferenceproxy; the public interface is the command.
answers.what: The inference proxy's rename proof measures that bin/cairn resolves the name inference to cairn/devices/inferenceproxy by running bin/cairn in a scratch HOME, instead of pinning bin/cairn's source text.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-18: 78a600419a21's land at 732da454b reddened cairn/devices/inferenceproxy/proofs/test_the_proxy_stands_at_its_outline_address.py through a text pin on bin/cairn's source. The behaviour (inference resolves to inferenceproxy) is not shown to have changed.

A text pin on another component's source is RULE 1 coupling in another form: it reds the pinned component's own changes at a third component's proof. This is the third cross-component red landed by a PROVED ticket today (dda0, 6eb2 via the docstring, 78a6).
